[0.072, "o", "\r\n:: The firewallD components & utilities have now been split into different packages:\r\n\r\n   - firewalld: Firewall daemon with D-Bus interface \r\n   - python-firewall: Python bindings for firewallD\r\n   - firewall-config: Graphical user interface for firewallD\r\n   - firewall-applet: Systray applet for firewallD\r\n"]
[0.003, "o", "   - firewalld-test: FirewallD test suite\r\n\r\n   Make sure to install the ones you may want / need.\r\n\r\nOptional dependencies for firewalld\r\n\u001b[0;1m   \u001b[0m bash-completion: bash completion\r\n    networkmanager: NetworkManager support\r\n    polkit: privileged actions\r\n    firewall-config: Graphical user interface for firewallD configuration\r\n    firewall-applet: Systray applet for firewallD\r\n    firewalld-test: firewallD test suite\r\n"]

[0.001, "o", "\u001b[?25l\u001b[m\u000f# vim:set ft=sh:\u001b[K\r\n# MODULES\u001b[K\r\n# The following modules are loaded before any boot hooks are\u001b[K\r\n# run.  Advanced users may wish to specify all system modules\u001b[K\r\n# in this array.  For instance:\u001b[K\r\n#     MODULES=(usbhid xhci_hcd)\u001b[K\r\nMODULES=()\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[K\n# BINARIES\u001b[K\r\n# This setting includes any additional binaries a given user may\u001b[K\r\n# wish into the CPIO image.  This is run last, so it may be used to\u001b[K\r\n# override the actual binaries included by a given hook\u001b[K\r\n# BINARIES are dependency parsed, so you may safely ignore libraries\u001b[K\r\nBINARIES=()\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[K\n# FILES\u001b[K\r\n# This setting is similar to BINARIES above, however, files are added\u001b[K\r\n# as-is and are not parsed in any way.  This is useful for config files.\u001b[K\r\nFILES=()\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[K\n# HOOKS\u001b[K\r\n# This is the most important setting in this file.  The HOOKS control the\u001b[K\r\n# modules and scripts added to the image, and what happens at boot time.\u001b[K\r\n# Order is important, and it is recommended that you do not change the\u001b[K\r\n# order in which HOOKS are added.  Run 'mkinitcpio -H <hook name>' for\u001b[K\r\n# help on a given hook.\u001b[K\r\n# 'base' is _required_ unless you know precisely what you are doing.\u001b[K\r\n# 'udev' is _required_ in order to automatically load modules\u001b[K\r\n# 'filesystems' is _required_ unless you specify your fs modules in MODULES\u001b[K\r\n# Examples:\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup specifies all modules in the MODULES setting above.\u001b[K\r\n##   No RAID, lvm2, or encrypted root is needed.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup will autodetect all modules for your system and should\u001b[K\r\n##   work as a sane default\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base udev autodetect microcode modconf block filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup will generate a 'full' image which supports most systems.\u001b[K\r\n##   No autodetection is done.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base udev microcode modconf block filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup assembles a mdadm array with an encrypted root file system.\u001b[K\r\n##   Note: See 'mkinitcpio -H mdadm_udev' for more information on RAID devices.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base udev microcode modconf keyboard keymap consolefont block mdadm_udev encrypt filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup loads an lvm2 volume group.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base udev microcode modconf block lvm2 filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This will create a systemd based initramfs which loads an encrypted root filesystem.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block sd-encrypt filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   NOTE: If you have /usr on a separate partition, you MUST include the\u001b[K\r\n#    usr and fsck hooks.\u001b[K\r\nHOOKS=(base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[K\n# COMPRESSION\u001b[K\r\n# Use this to compress the initramfs image. By default, zstd compression\u001b[K\r\n# is used for Linux ≥\u001b[59;22H 5.9 and gzip compression is used for Linux < 5.9.\u001b[K\r\n# Use 'cat' to create an uncompressed image.\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"zstd\"\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"gzip\"\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"bzip2\"\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"lzma\"\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"xz\"\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[0;10;7m\u000f/etc/mkinitcpio.d/default.conf                                                                                                                                                                                                1,1            Top\u001b[m\u000f\r\n\u001b[J\u001b[2 q\u001b[2 q\u001b[H# vim:set ft=sh:\u001b[K\r\n# MODULES\u001b[K\r\n# The following modules are loaded before any boot hooks are\u001b[K\r\n# run.  Advanced users may wish to specify all system modules\u001b[K\r\n# in this array.  For instance:\u001b[K\r\n#     MODULES=(usbhid xhci_hcd)\u001b[K\r\nMODULES=()\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[K\n# BINARIES\u001b[K\r\n# This setting includes any additional binaries a given user may\u001b[K\r\n# wish into the CPIO image.  This is run last, so it may be used to\u001b[K\r\n# override the actual binaries included by a given hook\u001b[K\r\n# BINARIES are dependency parsed, so you may safely ignore libraries\u001b[K\r\nBINARIES=()\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[K\n# FILES\u001b[K\r\n# This setting is similar to BINARIES above, however, files are added\u001b[K\r\n# as-is and are not parsed in any way.  This is useful for config files.\u001b[K\r\nFILES=()\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[K\n# HOOKS\u001b[K\r\n# Thi"]

The HOOKS control the\u001b[K\r\n# modules and scripts added to the image, and what happens at boot time.\u001b[K\r\n# Order is important, and it is recommended that you do not change the\u001b[K\r\n# order in which HOOKS are added.  Run 'mkinitcpio -H <hook name>' for\u001b[K\r\n# help on a given hook.\u001b[K\r\n# 'base' is _required_ unless you know precisely what you are doing.\u001b[K\r\n# 'udev' is _required_ in order to automatically load modules\u001b[K\r\n# 'filesystems' is _required_ unless you specify your fs modules in MODULES\u001b[K\r\n# Examples:\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup specifies all modules in the MODULES setting above.\u001b[K\r\n##   No RAID, lvm2, or encrypted root is needed.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup will autodetect all modules for your system and should\u001b[K\r\n##   work as a sane default\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base udev autodetect microcode modconf block filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup will generate a 'full' image which supports most systems.\u001b[K\r\n##   No autodetection is done.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base udev microcode modconf block filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup assembles a mdadm array with an encrypted root file system.\u001b[K\r\n##   Note: See 'mkinitcpio -H mdadm_udev' for more information on RAID devices.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base udev microcode modconf keyboard keymap consolefont block mdadm_udev encrypt filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This setup loads an lvm2 volume group.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base udev microcode modconf block lvm2 filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   This will create a systemd based initramfs which loads an encrypted root filesystem.\u001b[K\r\n#    HOOKS=(base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block sd-encrypt filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n#\u001b[K\r\n##   NOTE: If you have /usr on a separate partition, you MUST include the\u001b[K\r\n#    usr and fsck hooks.\u001b[K\r\nHOOKS=(base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block filesystems fsck)\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[K\n# COMPRESSION\u001b[K\r\n# Use this to compress the initramfs image. By default, zstd compression\u001b[K\r\n# is used for Linux ≥\u001b[59;22H 5.9 and gzip compression is used for Linux < 5.9.\u001b[K\r\n# Use 'cat' to create an uncompressed image.\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"zstd\"\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"gzip\"\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"bzip2\"\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"lzma\"\u001b[K\r\n#COMPRESSION=\"xz\"\u001b[K\r\n\u001b[0;10;7m\u000f/etc/mkinitcpio.d/default.conf                                                                                                                                                                                                1,1            Top\u001b[m\u000f\r\n\u001b[J\u001b[H\u001b[?25h\u001bP+q4D73\u001b\\"]
